🎙
Remarks and answers to questions
by Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at a working meeting with heads of leading African media outlets
(Moscow, October 27, 2026)
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
Our relations are growing
deeper and richer
with every passing day – indeed, with every passing hour.
We regard the African continent as a distinct civilisation and one of the key pillars of the
#MultipolarWorld
now taking shape on the international stage through the natural course of history, replacing the hegemony exercised by Western countries for more than 500 years.
🌍
Africa’s role as
one of the key pillars of this polycentric world order
is clearly reflected in
the Foreign Policy Concept of the Russian Federation
, approved by President
Vladimir Putin
in March 2023.
Russia is committed to strengthening equal, mutually beneficial relations
aimed at helping African countries build their own industrial base and enhancing Africa’s independence in the global economy, finance and technology. More broadly,
we seek to help our African friends consolidate their sovereignty
We do so in full accordance with
the principles of the UN Charter
, including
equality, mutual respect and non-interference in internal affairs
.
We strive, to the fullest extent possible,
to continue the work that the Soviet Union
, the predecessor of the Russian Federation,
carried out immediately following
decolonisation
: laying the foundations of national industry and the social sector in many African countries and making a substantial contribution to strengthening our African friends’ defence capabilities.
***
Other key points
:
•
Egypt is our key partner in the Middle East
in addressing security issues and tackling challenges and threats.
These, incidentally, became significantly more acute and widespread following the “Arab Spring” and, before that,
the US invasion of Iraq
and a series of other ventures, including in Libya and Syria, which fuelled refugee flows and spawned new terrorist organisations.
☝️
All our friends in the Middle East now have to contend with these consequences.
• Some members of Western elites disregard the interests of their own peoples and countries. They have declared Russia an adversary –
some even an outright enemy
. This certainly does not help foster normal international relations.
👉
In effect, it condemns the West to isolation, excluding it from promising multilateral initiatives that are now shaping the agenda for the future.
•
The West is convinced that it has the right to label others and that everyone else must listen
. This is the logic of former EU foreign policy chief
Josep Borrell
, who proudly described Europe as
a flourishing garden surrounded by a jungle
that must be fought. We can now see what kind of “flourishing garden” this is in footage of events unfolding in Paris and several other capitals.
•
The information war will continue and, I would even say, is tending to intensify.
Especially now, when, for example, US President
Donald Trump’s administration
, despite all its actions in support of Ukraine (supplying weapons sold to the Europeans and providing satellite intelligence) is
open to dialogue with us
and openly advocates expanding and deepening that dialogue to cover as many areas as possible.
•
Disinformation is what the West is still using, in a desperate effort, to keep its public on side.
But the demonstrations and protests show how difficult this has become. It is trying to convince people that they must sacrifice everything – wages, jobs, healthcare and social benefits – so that Ukraine can “defeat” Russia.
•
The information war is the very weapon the West is using to try to stay afloat.
But it is working less and less effectively. First, because people in European countries can feel their living conditions deteriorating.
🤝
Second, because our joint efforts in the information sphere are clearly delivering results
.
Read in full
#RussiaAfrica

.
Another telling episode involves
Masato Shinohara
, head of Fuji Television’s Seoul bureau. In 1993, he became
the subject of a criminal case in South Korea involving the acquisition of classified military documents
.
According to official South Korean records
, some of the information he collected was passed to a representative of the Japanese Embassy – its military attaché.
***
Now, back to
the present case
.
On October 13, 2026,
Russia’s FSB announced
that it had detained a Hokkaido Shimbun correspondent on Sakhalin on
suspicion of gathering information about Russia’s defence capabilities
on instructions from Japanese intelligence. The newspaper denies acting on government orders. What else would it say? As Westerners like to put it in such cases,
“You did it because you’ve done it before”
.
While I do not subscribe to that logic, I will send it back to its authors via Tokyo
))
Here in Russia, the court will give
the final legal assessment
of the circumstances of the case.
As for Japanese commentators who so confidently claim that being a journalist inherently rules out involvement in intelligence activities, t
hey would do well to familiarise themselves with their own history first.
Kuroi’s book
was published in Tokyo,
Sugishima’s account
appeared in the Japanese press, and his case was even discussed in the Japanese parliament.
So the question is not whether a Japanese journalist can work for the intelligence services.
History makes it abundantly clear: they can, and they do.
Why, then, are Japanese journalists expressing such theatrical astonishment at their colleague’s arrest?
👉
They should direct all their indignation at their own leaders – official Tokyo and its Western handlers.

⚡️
Russian MFA statement on personal sanctions against executives of British defence companies
(October 27, 2026)
In response to
London’s hostile anti-Russian policy
, which includes stepped-up efforts to flood Zelensky’s neo-Nazi clique with weapons,
a decision has been taken to add several executives of British defence companies to Russia’s entry ban list
. These companies supply the Kiev regime with weapons and military technologies used to strike deep inside Russia.
Clearly, the massive supplies of missiles, drones and related technologies to Ukrainian thugs serve a single purpose –
to inflict maximum damage on our country
.
The British narrative of a supposed
“defence dividend”
for their own military-industrial complex only highlights their
purely exploitative and opportunistic approach to Ukraine
, whose statehood is being sacrificed, in part, to generate profits for private British companies and their lobbyists.
Meanwhile, the funds that Andy Burnham’s government is channelling into military contractors’ projects that bring death and destruction
could be put to use in the UK civilian sector, where the crisis is deepening
as a result of mistakes by successive British governments that are eroding the country’s social fabric.
The ruling Labour party
, however, whose Russophobic obsession differs little from that of its Conservative predecessors,
apparently has very different budget priorities.
❌
The following British nationals are now barred from entering the Russian Federation:
•
HEAD, Alex Edward
– CEO of Rotron Aerospace, a company participating in the Brakestop long-range missile development project;

,

,

,

Work to expand Russia’s stop list in response to the hostile actions of the British authorities will continue.

(Moscow, October 27, 2026)
💬
Vladimir Putin:
We greatly appreciate your personal, active participation in
the #RussiaAfrica Summit
.
It is important that Mozambique was also represented at the highest level at
the previous Russia–Africa forums
, which, in my view, laid
a solid foundation for developing Russia’s ties with the entire continent.
Today, we worked productively together at
the 8th Gas Exporting Countries Forum Summit
.
🇷🇺
🇲🇿
We fully share your commitment to strengthening the multifaceted ties between our countries.
Russia and Mozambique enjoy longstanding bonds of friendship and cooperation dating back to
the Mozambican people’s struggle for independence
. Last year, we marked a significant milestone –
the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations
.
Political contacts and interparliamentary ties are developing
. In September, delegations of Mozambican parliamentarians took part in the election observation mission for
Russia’s State Duma elections
.
📈
Trade and economic cooperation is growing stronger.
Bilateral trade
nearly doubled
in January-August this year. Our
Intergovernmental Commission
is actively working and held its fourth meeting in Moscow recently, on October 1.
We traditionally enjoy close ties in education
. This year, we welcomed Mozambican civil servants for training for the first time. The quota for students from your country to study at Russian universities at the expense of the federal budget
continues to grow steadily
.
We will also continue to provide humanitarian assistance to Mozambique.
As you know, this spring,
Russia’s EMERCOM delivered humanitarian aid
to help address the aftermath of flooding caused by Cyclone Gezani.
🤝
Our cooperation at multilateral international platforms, above all the UN, is constructive.
We are grateful for Mozambique’s support for many Russian initiatives and its rejection of outrageous Russophobic actions.
#RussiaMozambique

.

and
VTB

I would also highlight our closer coordination on the international stage
, given Qatar’s important mediation role in resolving various crises, including in the Persian Gulf region.
As you know, Your Highness, from the very outset of
the conflict surrounding Iran
,
Russia has advocated an end to hostilities and a political and diplomatic solution
.
The Islamabad Memorandum
, signed in June through Qatari and Pakistani mediation, remains relevant as a basis for advancing the negotiating process.
☝️
For our part, we are ready to do everything within our power to help resolve this complex and acute crisis
.
🇷🇺
🇶🇦
#RussiaQatar

item.title: 🇷🇺 On October 27, Foreign Minister of Russia Sergey Lavrov and Minister of State, Minister of Foreign Affairs, National Community Abroad and African Affairs of Algeria Ahmed Attaf
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇩🇿 On October 27, Foreign Minister of Russia Sergey Lavrov and Minister of State, Minister of Foreign Affairs, National Community Abroad and African Affairs of Algeria Ahmed Attaf held a meeting in Moscow . Ahmed Attaf arrived as part of the delegation led by Algerian Prime Minister Sifi Ghrieb to attend the 8th Gas Exporting Countries Forum Summit and the Third #RussiaAfrica Summit . 👉 Sergey Lavrov's opening remarks The Ministers held substantive discussions on practical steps to strengthen the enhanced strategic partnership between Russia and Algeria. They expressed satisfaction with the trust underpinning their political dialogue and their well-established cooperation, both bilaterally and at multilateral platforms , including the UN. Following an exchange of views on developments in North Africa and the Sahara-Sahel region, the Sides reaffirmed their shared interest in continuing effective Russian-Algerian coordination to resolve ongoing conflicts through political and diplomatic means , based on universally recognised principles of international law and the UN Charter . #RussiaAlgeria
